jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original professional HAND-DRAWN CONCEPT sheet, 1536x1024 landscape, ivory paper, crisp pencil/ink, light construction lines, restrained colored markers. Same design family as the GUIHANG mother ship in input image 1: warm-white panels, blue-gray thick structure, graphite mechanical recesses, sparse brick-red identity blocks, local amber work lights, serviceable modular parts. No photoreal CGI, no generic luxury spacecraft, no random glowing holograms, no dimension claims, no dense fake text. This is concept development before Blender, not an engineering drawing.
Asset: the compact protected COMMAND BRIDGE inside the small aft command island of this exact ship. Upper 65 percent is one rich interior perspective from the rear looking forward. Six to eight functional workstations in a modest room, not an auditorium. Two forward navigation/port-control seats, four midroom operator consoles, one compact aft coordination desk. Small thick recessed observation windows, more emphasis on physical inset instrument panels and clean limited displays than giant panoramic glass. UI is abstract quiet blocks, no readable paragraphs. Rigid seat frames with lap/shoulder restraints, foot captures and grabrails make axial LOW-GRAVITY operation legible. Crew are seated and restrained or attached to rails, no free-standing coffee cups. Walk/handhold passages at both sides, two identifiable rear pressure doors and a maintenance access hatch. Warm light on faces, equipment lights subtle. One inactive station under a fabric cover, a tiny clipped personal photograph and an unfinished shift card give human history.
Bottom left: simple top-down PLAN of the SAME room with matching seat count, forward window strip, side passages and two aft doors.
Bottom right: exploded side-detail of ONE operator station in four visually connected layers: structural pedestal/foot restraint, seat frame and harness, cushioning, hinged control console and under-seat service connector; plus a tiny wall slice showing outside armor, pressure shell and inner equipment lining. Parts have dotted assembly lines; no invented zero-g chair floating without mounts.
Labels only BRIDGE / PLAN / OPERATOR STATION / PRESSURE SHELL. Preserve a restrained naval industrial mood; people are small and ordinary, no franchise uniforms or emblems.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original professional HAND-DRAWN CONCEPT sheet, 1536x1024 landscape, ivory paper, crisp pencil/ink, light construction lines, restrained colored markers. Same design family as the GUIHANG mother ship in input image 1: warm-white panels, blue-gray thick structure, graphite mechanical recesses, sparse brick-red identity blocks, local amber work lights, serviceable modular parts. No photoreal CGI, no generic luxury spacecraft, no random glowing holograms, no dimension claims, no dense fake text. This is concept development before Blender, not an engineering drawing.
Asset: a communal room inside the ark's enclosed ROTATING HABITAT candidate, intimate human life, not a luxury liner. Upper 65 percent: one human-eye-level interior perspective. A long narrow modular room with subtle curved deck and repeating structural ribs, eight seats around one shared table, seven simple meal settings, a food-service niche, storage wall and an ordinary sealed door leading to an unawakened residential sector. No huge exterior window: room is deep inside protected hull. Small porthole into another pressurized circulation corridor only. Lit active half uses warm white panels, worn composite tabletop, fabric acoustic pads and a few repaired cup straps; closed sector beyond the far door stays cool and quiet. Show two or three ordinary crew in maintenance clothes sharing work/food, no royalty, no magic technology. Trays and cups have modest anti-spill clips. A folded garment and a repaired textile sleeve make it feel like a lived-in home. Thin brick-red door identification panel, physically attached rail lights.
Bottom left: plain PLAN, eight-seat table in center, service niche and lockers along one wall, entry on one end and sealed sector door opposite. Plan must match main perspective rather than invent another room.
Bottom center: tiny section diagram showing the room on the INNER curved deck of an ENCLOSED rotating drum inside a nonrotating hull. Its floor's outward radial direction is clear. A central nonrotating service spine and a small controlled transfer vestibule are distinct; do not connect ordinary doors directly between incompatible rotating structures. This is a schematic conceptual relationship, not solved bearings.
Bottom right: exploded TABLE assembly with anchored serviceable base, replaceable slab, removable tray/cup clips, underside service-light rail, dotted assembly guides. No houseplants, decorative trees, chandeliers, glass city dome or balconies.
Labels only COMMON ROOM / PLAN / HABITAT SECTION / TABLE MODULE. Mood: a few people slowly bringing a vast ship back to life.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Derive a HAND-DRAWN mechanical concept sheet of the SENTINEL humanoid ONLY from the CENTER machine in input image 1. The reference contains three roles: do NOT redesign the explorer or harvester here. Preserve Sentinel's low flattened hornless head, amber visor recessed in high collar, broad wrapping chest shell and shoulder roots, exposed compact mechanical waist, thick shins, dark knees, short wide feet, warm-white/navy/graphite with sparse brick red. Its LEFT arm carries the same long tool-shield; RIGHT hand the same lowered fictional carbine. Original design, no new V-fin, crown, crystal or decorative wings.
Purpose: resolve the back-equipment ambiguity and explain parts, not a second armor variant.
1536x1024 ivory drawing paper, crisp ink/pencil with muted marker shading. Three main panels:
LEFT: clear full-body FRONT view of the exact same Sentinel, neutral stance, consistent armor shapes.
CENTER: full-body BACK view of the same Sentinel, showing exactly TWO main compact maneuvering pods mounted symmetrically high left and right. Between them is a clearly visible CENTRAL capture saddle, lower than the pod tops, with two mechanical locking lugs and an unobstructed approach path from behind. A protected service connector sits below the saddle. Do not fill that space with a third giant thruster or spine backpack.
RIGHT: exploded three-quarter arrangement of the SAME machine with armored torso shells and shoulder/shin plates displaced only a little from an unarmored mechanical skeleton, the TWO back pods displaced to the sides, central saddle and shield/carbine as separate attached-system parts, dotted guides back to mounting locations. Do not add extra arms or legs, duplicate head or turn the skeleton into a human.
Small lower-right inset: closer saddle/paired locks and disconnected service plug, showing plug attaches only after mechanical capture. Number ONLY four back elements consistently across back and exploded drawings: 1 left pod, 2 right pod, 3 central saddle, 4 service plug. Labels only FRONT / BACK / SYSTEM BREAKDOWN / CAPTURE INTERFACE. No fake dimension text. Keep upper armor silhouette coherent across all three panels; left and right are the machine's own sides. This is a concept assembly, not validated engineering, rigging or weapon construction.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Derive an ORIGINAL HAND-DRAWN mechanical assembly study from the LEFT EXPLORER and RIGHT HARVESTER in input image 1, preserving their identity. Do not include the humanoid center machine. 1536x1024 ivory drafting paper, pencil/ink and quiet colored marker, warm-white armor, slate blue-gray structure, graphite joints, brick-red identity patches, amber tool warnings. Make two generous columns.
LEFT EXPLORER: show its compact horizontal optical-black sensor face, two articulated sensing outriggers, two sampling claws and short docking skids in a large three-quarter EXPLODED VIEW. Separate only four logical groups by modest distances and dashed assembly lines: upper protective armor, central sensor/chassis core, outrigger/claw mechanisms, twin compact maneuver modules and belly capture saddle. Underneath show the SAME machine in deployed and folded service states. The black sensor-face band must remain IDENTIFIABLE in both; if partly protected during folding, show the actual protective shutter and a simple motion arrow, not an unexplained new face. Arms fold toward the same chassis; no missing or extra appendages.
RIGHT HARVESTER: show the SAME low heavy work core, EXACTLY FOUR main working arms (two thick anchoring clamp arms, two secondary tool arms with cutter and gripper), small rear stabilizing legs, removable rear ore cassette. Explode the upper armor and ore cassette upward and tool tips outward, keep all arm roots attached to the central structural chassis. Show one detailed detachable tool-head mount with paired clamps, retained connector and a load path, plus a small cassette exchange sketch showing one empty dock and the SAME cassette moving along guide rails. Do not double the number of arms or make the ore bin a separate spaceship.
Across bottom center: a shared original rectangular capture saddle, paired locking lugs, tow attachment and covered service port, repeated on both machines in matching relative belly locations. Keep assembly lines clean, no dimension claims, no exact manufacturing specs, no tiny paragraphs. Labels only EXPLORER / HARVESTER / DEPLOYED / STOWED / TOOL INTERFACE / SHARED CAPTURE. Show real mechanical relationships at concept level, not decorative floating parts.
